t: Wadai was an Islamic sultanate in what is now eastern Chad, founded in the early 17th century after a revolt against the Tunjur.
Its caravan road to Benghazi made it a major trans-Saharan trading power, fed largely by slave raiding into the lands to the south.
Weakened by succession wars, it fell to the French, who took Abéché in 1909 and abolished the sultanate in 1912.
dyk: The Anglo-French convention of 1899 assigned Wadai to France and Darfur to Britain, a division that still broadly underlies the Chad-Sudan border.
ev: Abd al-Karim ibn Jama overthrows the Tunjur and founds the Wadai sultanate at Wara
Sultan Sabun begins his reign and opens a caravan route through Kufra to Benghazi
Sultan Muhammad al-Sharif moves the capital from Wara to Abéché
Sultan Ali's armies sack Massenya, capital of the rival sultanate of Bagirmi
An Anglo-French convention places Wadai in the French sphere
A French column captures Abéché and installs Adam Asil as a client sultan
Sultan Dud Murra surrenders after years of resistance from the countryside
